construct: Activated osteoclasts form a sealed resorption lacuna beneath the ruffled border. Carbonic anhydrase II generates intracellular H+ and bicarbonate; vacuolar H+-ATPases pump H+ across the ruffled border, while chloride transport maintains electroneutrality. Acid dissolves hydroxyapatite, allowing proteases to degrade organic matrix.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Osteoclasts acidify the sealed resorption lacuna using ruffled-border vacuolar H+-ATPases; the low pH dissolves hydroxyapatite.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Na/K ATPase is important for cell homeostasis, but it does not directly pump protons into the resorption lacuna; bicarbonate secretion would oppose acidification.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Normal osteoclast number with isolated failure to acidify the ruffled-border compartment uniquely points to V-H+-ATPase proton secretion.
